column1: # Game profile of Slay the Spire (Switch, base game 1.0). Plays on the Mac (see README.md)
# Mega Crit's libGDX (Java) game on MonoGame.Switch, compiled ahead of time to native code by BRUTE (main holds the paths MonoGame.Switch/Brute/mono/mscorlib/... and the class
# BRUTE.Runtime; its managed strings, com.badlogic.gdx among them, are UTF-16). It renders with NVIDIA's desktop OpenGL through EGL: main takes every GL call from eglGetProcAddress,
# by names it keeps as UTF-16 strings (glShaderSource among them, never as C text), which the host's GL layer answers on Metal (dm/gfx/gl/hle_gl.m), so NVIDIA's GL driver (subsdk0)
# The shaders are the GLSL files in the RomFS's shaders/ folder (7 .vs and 7 .fs, as libGDX names them; 11 distinct), which dm/gfx/tools/gl_shaders.py translates offline;
# a capture run with an empty library showed the game compiles exactly these, so it needs no capture table
# main imports the EGL functions only, so NVIDIA's GL driver (subsdk0, NintendoSDK_OpenGL) stays unloaded
# main sets a heap of at most the pool − 64 MB: a 3328 MB heap region
# the NPDM declares no system resource, so IsVirtualAddressMemoryEnabled is false, as on hardware
# no NVN shaders: the profile's NVN tables stay empty and the GL library comes from gl_shaders.py (the RomFS's .vs / .fs files and gl_capture.tsv)

column2: Slay the Spire's shaders: libGDX's .vs / .fs files in the RomFS and its built-in ones, captured on the Mac; translated by gl_shaders.py, no NVN tables
